Iris Fœtidissima.

Iris fœtidissima. N. O. Iridaceæ. Tincture of root.

Clinical.─Headache. Hernia.

Characteristics.─Ir. fœt. was proved under Berridge's direction. One prover, Dr. Croker, chewed a piece of the root; another took the tincture; one experienced symptoms from potentising the drug, and later took the 14th dilution. The rest took very high potencies. The prover who chewed the root experienced a burning feeling in mouth and fauces extending to stomach, and not relieved by cold water or anything else. A number of pains were felt in the head.

Relations.─Compare: The Arums and the other Irises.

SYMPTOMS.

1. Mind.─Makes mistakes in writing and speaking; puts "right" for "left" and vice versâ.
